preregistered.prior_claude: Bitwise identical across co-location. Reason: batch size 1, seeded CUDA generator, cuDNN deterministic with benchmark off, folding DP on the CPU. The most likely way it fails: with benchmark off, cuDNN still picks algorithms heuristically and that choice can depend on free workspace memory, which co-location changes; cuBLAS runs without CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG; atomics in some backward kernels.
preregistered.rule_user: If training is bitwise deterministic the floor is exactly zero. If it is not, every later seed-variance figure is reported against this floor.
preregistered.ten_epoch_pairs: the full study adds one duplicate per weight arm on the OTHER GPU, in a different wave, so the floor is also measured at epoch 10
preregistered.what: One seed (the first recorded seed) trained twice under deliberately different GPU co-location, compared with each other and with its original epoch-1 run.

events.cause: As far as known: the phase-full driver ran as a background shell of a Claude Code session, and that session's process ended at about 05:59:22 on 2026-10-09 (its transcript records a pending question torn down at 09:59:22 UTC), 2 s after the driver's last artifact write; a process that ends takes its background shells and their children with it. No reboot (the machine has been up since 2026-09-30 15:08), and the gauge launcher, started detached with setsid, kept running and passed its gate at 06:00:04. Not established: which signal ended the processes, or why the session ended. The six runs' stdout logs are empty because their block-buffered output was lost when they were killed, so the logs hold no evidence either way; their attempts carry no exit code because the driver died before it could poll them.
events.remedy: The six were rerun FRESH, from initialisation for 10 continuous epochs, with their registered seeds, weights and GPUs and in their registered run directories, under the registered no-resume policy (full_study.design.why_fresh_not_resumed); they were NOT resumed from their partial checkpoints. The partial directories were moved, unchanged, to interrupted_2026-10-09/. The rerun driver runs as its own session leader (setsid), so no terminal or agent session can end it.

stopped.bound: the driver rewrites the artifact every 30 s, so it stopped within 30 s after its last write

detected_as.detail: processes gone while status is RUNNING

events.unaffected: the other 12 runs had reached epoch 10 and are kept as they are

design.concurrency: at most 3 processes per GPU (6 at once); a freed slot starts the next queued run on that GPU
design.cpu_contention: the family-matched Rfam control may run concurrently with a thread cap; timing is not a deliverable of this phase
design.oom_policy: a run that fails is restarted from scratch at most 1 time(s); every attempt is recorded
design.pairing: data order, initialisation and dropout draws depend only on the seed (the same number of generator draws per step in both arms), so each seed is a paired comparison between the two weights
design.placement: seed i, weight w -> GPU (i + arm index) mod 2, so each GPU carries 4 runs of each arm; duplicates on the GPU opposite their original, queued last
design.runs: 2 weights x 8 seeds, each a FRESH continuous 10-epoch `mxfold2 train` run, plus one duplicate per weight (determinism floor at epoch 10): 18 runs
design.why_fresh_not_resumed: MXfold2's --resume re-seeds torch at start and restores no RNG state (train.py Train.run), so a resumed epoch 2 replays epoch 1's shuffle order and dropout masks exactly. Continuing the epoch-1 checkpoints would not be MXfold2's own 10-epoch run. The epoch-1 checkpoints serve timing and the determinism control.

notes: folding factors divide MXfold2's fold time, measured with 8 training processes running, by ViennaRNA's, measured alone on one pinned core: contention can only inflate them
nn_forward and backward include CUDA synchronisation; the first step of each process includes CUDA warm-up

projection_correction: Correction recorded 2026-10-08, BEFORE any decomposition is computed. The protocol states that h is orthogonal to every g_p (h.g_p = 1 - 1 = 0). That holds only for pairs where both S_in(i,j) and S_out(j,i) exist. A pair that can stack on one side only, e.g. i = 1 (no outside stack), has h.g_p = +1 or -1. P_G is therefore computed with h replaced by h' = h - sum_p (h.g_p / g_p.g_p) g_p (Gram-Schmidt). The span G(x), every prediction and every other definition are unchanged; this fixes the arithmetic, not the question.
protocol:
DESIGN (fixed before any training; written to metrics.json before any launch)

Model     MixC, the architecture of the released model (vendor/mxfold2 at 51b2136,
          models/TrainSetAB.conf without its --param line), built in .venv-mxfold2 with
          torch 2.13.0+cu130 and numpy 2.4.6. MXfold2 pins torch ^1.4 and numpy ^1.18;
          both pins are overridden, and the one-batch smoke test under these versions
          passed before this study was written.
Training  bpRNA-1m TR0 (canonical-pair version, 10,814 sequences) UNCAPPED, from the
          registered MXfold2 datasets (data/SOURCES.yaml: mxfold2_datasets). Chosen over
          TrainSetA+B capped at 400 nt because it is a complete published dataset (no
          subset to defend), it comes with a published test split for a disjoint fixed
          evaluation set, and the cap would save only ~13% of its folding time.
Arms      --loss-func hinge_mix (the loss that contains the thermodynamic regulariser
          sl_weight * (ref - ref2)^2 / L) at --score-loss-weight 1.0 (the code default
          value) and 0.125 (the paper's C1). The weight is the only difference between
          arms. (The code's default LOSS is plain hinge, with no regulariser at all.)
Seeds     the 8 SEEDS of scripts/pooled_alignment.py, read from its source.
Epochs    10 planned, the code default; the paper does not state an epoch count.
Other     every other hyperparameter at the code default: AdamW, lr 1e-3, batch 1,
          loss-pos-paired 0.5 and loss-neg-paired 0.005 (the paper's delta values),
          l1-weight 0, l2 inactive in the code.
Hardware  4 seeds per GPU on both TITAN RTXs, one CPU thread per process.

EVALUATION SET: all 1,305 sequences of TS0 (canonical-pair version), listed in
metrics.json by file name, length and sha256 of the sequence.

DECOMPOSITION (pre-registered; run after training, not in this phase)

For evaluation sequence x (length N), trained model k (seed) at weight w, theta_k(x) is
the vector of MXfold2's positional outputs that some structure of x can use, plus the
global helix_length table:
  S_in(i,j)  = score_helix_stacking[i][j], i<j, (i,j) and (i+1,j-1) both allowed pairs
  S_out(j,i) = score_helix_stacking[j][i], (i,j) and (i-1,j+1) both allowed pairs
  M_in(i,j)  = score_mismatch[i][j], M_out(j,i) = score_mismatch[j][i], (i,j) allowed
  U(a,b)     = the unpaired-interval score, 1 <= a <= b <= N
  helix_length[1..30]
where an allowed pair is canonical (AU, UA, GC, CG, GU, UG) with at least 3 unpaired
nucleotides between, as MXfold2's own constraint builder sets it.
The exact gauge subspace G(x) (scripts/mxfold2_nullspace.py, step 2) is spanned by
  g_p (one per allowed pair p=(i,j)): +1 on S_in(i,j) and M_in(i,j), -1 on S_out(j,i)
       and M_out(j,i), wherever those entries exist;
  h: +1 on every S entry, -2(m-1) on helix_length[m].
These are mutually orthogonal (disjoint supports; h.g_p = 1 - 1 = 0), so the projection
P_G is closed-form. With Delta_k = theta_k(x) - mean over the 8 seeds:
  V_G(x,w)   = (1/7) sum_k ||P_G Delta_k||^2      seed variance in the exact gauge
  V_tot(x,w) = (1/7) sum_k ||Delta_k||^2
  f_G(x,w)   = V_G / V_tot
V_G is a LOWER BOUND on null-space seed variance: step 2 found null directions beyond
G that it could not characterise. The trainable Turner half of MixC is global; its
seed variance is reported separately and not decomposed (that needs MXfold2's own
Turner counting rule, which has not been derived).

Validity checks, required before any statistic is reported:
  V1  the counting rule above, applied to the extracted tables, reproduces MXfold2's
      own positional score (MixC constrained score minus the Turner-only constrained
      score) of each evaluation sequence's reference structure to within
      1e-3 * max(1, |score|);
  V2  adding a random g in G(x) to a trained model's tables changes MXfold2's score of
      the reference and of the predicted structure by less than that tolerance;
  V3  a random direction orthogonal to G(x) changes at least one of them by more.

PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTIONS
  W1 (user). Null-space seed variance is the same at both weights, because step 2
     found the regulariser gauge-invariant. Test: r(x) = V_G(x,0.125) / V_G(x,1.0);
     "the same" means the 95% bootstrap interval (10,000 resamples over evaluation
     sequences, seed 20261006) of the median of log r lies inside [log 0.8, log 1.25].
  W2 (added by Claude, secondary). The per-sequence constant shift c_x (+(b-a+1) on
     U(a,b), +1 on every S and M entry; it moves every structure of x by exactly N) is
     invisible to the hinge loss and pinned only by the regulariser, so its seed
     variance is LARGER at 0.125 than at 1.0: median over x of the ratio > 1.

PHASE epoch1 (this file): weight 1.0 only, one epoch, then stop. Records the measured
per-step overhead and the measured folding factor (MXfold2's unconstrained fold time
over ViennaRNA MFE time on the same TR0 sequences, the latter measured here on an
idle pinned core before launch), replacing both guesses in the earlier estimate.
